gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the inverter's own idle draw is added to a 150 W pellet stove's load. When you include it (stove W + idle W), the 5,024 Wh Anker SOLIX S5000 (about 10 W idle) runs about 30 h. That matches the 6,144 Wh EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra (45–60 W idle, 29–31 h), and the Anker SOLIX F3800 falls from ChatGPT's 21.8 h to about 14 h because of its roughly 80 W idle draw.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT cited plus the top results I could open. ChatGPT's own answer divides capacity × 0.85 by 150 W and ignores idle draw. solarwaypoint.com's three-way comparison lists capacity and weight but no idle draw, efficiency or runtime. sparkpowered.com (2026-11-14) uses 85% of rated Wh and gives no idle draw. runtimemath.com (2026-11-14) works maker-listed self-draw into its runtimes only for the smaller BLUETTI/EcoFlow/Anker C-series units (Apex 300 at 20 W, for example). It has no idle figure for the DELTA Pro Ultra, DELTA Pro 3 or F3800, and gives the S5000 a flat 0.85 factor. Our current dealectric page has an idle figure only for the Elite 300 (19 W). Both cited enoughwatts.com pages failed to load (TLS certificate error), so I could not check them. No page I read runs the big units' measured delivered Wh against stove watts plus idle watts.
decides: For an actual pellet stove load (about 150 W), it changes ChatGPT's ranking. A bigger battery doesn't automatically mean a longer runtime, because a 45–80 W idle draw is 30–53% on top of the stove's draw. The DELTA Pro Ultra's 34.8 h shrinks to about 29–31 h, which is a tie with the S5000's ~30 h. The S5000 has less rated capacity but a 10 W idle draw, and it's already in our catalog (anker-solix-s5000). The F3800 drops from 21.8 h to about 14 h, behind the DELTA Pro 3 (up to 25 h). The DELTA Pro Ultra X with two batteries (12,288 Wh, about 36 W idle) still runs longest overall. Among single boxes, the S5000 and DELTA Pro Ultra are effectively tied, so price per hour should decide the pick. I could not source either price today.
